items.text: In his first address in Argentina, given to authorities, civil society and the diplomatic corps at the Palacio Libertad in Buenos Aires, Pope Leo XIV honored Pope Francis and urged leaders to treat authority as service and put the common good above immediate interests. He called for dialogue across political differences, stronger institutions against corruption and organized crime, economic growth that reaches the poor, the unemployed and the elderly, and asked why so many young Argentines feel they must leave. He also spoke for the unborn and the sick, care for natural resources, and the ethical responsibilities raised by new technology, especially artificial intelligence. President Javier Milei welcomed him with remarks recalling Pope Francis and the value of faith.

Pope Leo XIV sent a telegram, signed by Cardinal Pietro Parolin, to Cardinal Grzegorz Ryś of Kraków expressing his spiritual closeness to all affected by the Nov. 7 Main Market Square shooting that killed six and wounded fifteen. Cardinal Ryś celebrated a Sunday Mass for the victims at St. Anne's Church, moved from St. Mary's Basilica while the square was sealed, saying the final word cannot belong to hatred.

Pope Leo XIV left Uruguay on Sunday afternoon, telling Uruguayans he carries them in his heart, and landed at Buenos Aires' Aeroparque Jorge Newbery at 4:33 p.m. local time, where President Javier Milei greeted him at the foot of the plane. The evening schedule includes a tribute to General San Martín, a welcome ceremony and meeting with Milei at the Casa Rosada, and a visit to the Palacio Libertad. He remains in Argentina through Wednesday, Nov. 11, with stops in Córdoba and Luján, before leaving for Lima.

In Brazil, Bishop Canísio Klaus of Sinop issued a Nov. 3 pastoral letter stating that no public Mass according to the 1962 Roman Missal is authorized in his diocese under Traditionis custodes. He asks the faithful not to organize or attend unauthorized celebrations, calling them illicit though not necessarily invalid, and says simple attendance does not automatically incur excommunication, while formal adherence to a break with Rome can amount to schism.

Bishop Barry Knestout of Richmond, a member of the U.S. bishops' task force on human dignity in the age of artificial intelligence, wrote that the bishops "do not engage in fear mongering" but that human dignity must guide AI development. Drawing on Pope Leo XIV's encyclical Magnifica humanitas, he said the task force aims to offer moral and ethical guidance to the technology field and to advocate for legislation that keeps the human person at the center.

On his last day in Uruguay, Pope Leo XIV celebrated Mass at the National Shrine of Our Lady of the Thirty-Three in Florida. He recalled that those fighting for independence in 1825 entrusted the country's future to Mary before her image, and he renewed Uruguay's consecration to her, offering a Golden Rose. He thanked mothers and grandmothers who pass on the faith even when their children no longer practice it, asked fathers and grandfathers to let their children see that faith has a real place in a man's life, and told Uruguayans to go out again, enter people's homes, listen to their questions, and bring them to Christ.

Earlier Sunday morning he stopped at Saint Therese Parish in Juanico, the first parish in Uruguay dedicated to her after her canonization, and greeted about 2,000 people in the courtyard after praying inside the church. He said his family, especially his father, had a great devotion to Saint Therese, and he asked them not to be afraid to say, "I am a Christian, I am Catholic, I believe in Jesus Christ."

A gunman killed six people and wounded fifteen in Krakow's Main Market Square on Saturday, near St. Mary's Basilica. Cardinal Grzegorz Rys said the Church must stand together and that hatred cannot have the last word, and he invited the faithful to a Mass for the victims and the wounded. Archbishop Tadeusz Wojda, president of the Polish bishops' conference, said he stood in prayer with all who suffered.

Argentina's State Intelligence Secretariat (SIDE) said Saturday it had detained a person over death threats against Pope Leo XIV, on the eve of the Pope's arrival in the country. The arrest was ordered by a federal court in Campana.

Pope Leo XIV leaves Uruguay for Argentina today, the first papal visit there since 1987. He is due at Buenos Aires' Aeroparque at 4:30 p.m. local time, then visits the San Martín monument, is welcomed at the Casa Rosada and meets President Javier Milei. The Argentina stage runs through Nov. 11 with stops in Córdoba and Luján under the motto "Welcome everyone. Go and proclaim."

About 70,000 people filled Montevideo's Estadio Centenario for Saturday night's prayer vigil, where the Pope told Uruguay's Catholics not to fear being a minority and said Christ did not call them to mediocrity. One couple got engaged during the event.

At the Catholic University of Uruguay in Montevideo, Pope Leo XIV told educators that other people are a blessing, not a threat, and asked Catholic schools to help students recover their full dignity as persons. He urged schools and universities to make judicious use of technologies and AI, placing the person before the algorithm and harmonizing technical, emotional, social, spiritual and ecological intelligence.

At the evening prayer vigil in Centenario Stadium on his last night in Uruguay, the Pope told the faithful not to settle for a merely decent life or habitual faith. He urged young people to dare to marry and start families, couples to welcome children, and those called to the priesthood or consecrated life to answer without fear, and pointed them to prayer, Mass, Confession, the Gospel and Eucharistic adoration.

In the poor Casavalle neighborhood of Montevideo, Leo said Christians cannot turn a blind eye to injustice, naming children out of school, hungry families and violent crime, and asked the Church and civil authorities to work together to protect human dignity. Earlier he stopped at the Bishop Jacinto Vera Home for retired priests and thanked about 20 elderly priests for their years of ministry.

After the Paysandú Mass, Pope Leo XIV visited the Cathedral Basilica of Our Lady of the Rosary and St. Benedict of Palermo, unveiled a commemorative plaque, and greeted the faithful outside. He urged Uruguayans to build bridges that unite people in faith and peace, saying peace is possible and they want to build it, then returned by air to Montevideo.

In Montevideo on Saturday afternoon, Pope Leo XIV reached the Parish of Our Lady of Guadalupe in Casavalle, a marginalized neighborhood on the capital’s outskirts, accompanied by Cardinal Daniel Sturla. After a brief off-agenda stop at a priests’ residence, he was to meet the local social community, hear testimonies, and bless twelve homes in the parish’s Familias de Guadalupe housing project. Catholic University and the Estadio Centenario prayer vigil remain later in the day.

On Saturday morning in Paysandú, Pope Leo XIV celebrated his first Mass in South America at Parque París Londres before tens of thousands. In the homily he urged Uruguayans to be bridges so others meet Jesus, a fraternal community that shares life with those in need, and a community of prayer. He thanked God for Blessed Jacinto Vera, the gaucho bishop of Montevideo, and used local images of the border bridge, palm trees, and mate. Afternoon stops in Montevideo still ahead: Casavalle, the Catholic University, and the Centenario stadium vigil.

At the Builders AI Forum (Nov. 5–6) at Rome’s Pontifical Gregorian University, Cardinal Michael Czerny said everyone is impacted by AI but people are not listening to one another. New Communications prefect Montse Alvarado stressed that AI is a tool, not a person: the Gospel message is communicated through AI, not by it. Bishop Stephen Wang pointed to Magisterium AI in priestly formation; Hallow’s Erich Kerekes said prayer is a relationship AI cannot invent.

The Archdiocese of New Orleans added 27 deceased clergy to its list of priests credibly accused of child sexual abuse on Nov. 6, the largest update since the list was first published in 2018. Ten served as archdiocesan priests and 17 belonged to religious orders or other dioceses but were accused of abuse in the area. The list now holds 106 names. Archbishop James Checchio said the release is part of the $300 million bankruptcy settlement, which also provides for a public archive of clergy-abuse records at LSU, and that no clergy with a credible claim remain in ministry.

Pope Leo XIV closed his first day in Uruguay by greeting a crowd, many of them young people, outside the Apostolic Nunciature in Montevideo. In his Vespers homily with the country's bishops, clergy and religious, he held up Blessed Jacinto Vera, Montevideo's first bishop, as a defender of religious freedom. Saturday's program includes an evening vigil at Centenario Stadium.

The Archdiocese of Portland in Oregon's Office of Divine Worship, in its November newsletter, asked lay faithful and deacons not to extend their hands in the orans posture or hold hands during the Our Father at Mass, citing the General Instruction of the Roman Missal and canon law that reserve the gesture to the priest.

Pope Leo XIV completed his first day in Uruguay with a welcome at Plaza Independencia in Montevideo, an address to authorities, civil society, and the diplomatic corps, a meeting with President Yamandú Orsi, and Vespers at the Metropolitan Cathedral. In the Plaza address he spoke on the common good: protection of the unborn and support for families, care for children and the elderly, accessible health care, and a secular state that leaves room for believers and non-believers to live together without confining religion to the private sphere. Local authorities estimated about 30,000 people along the route and in the square.

At Vespers with bishops, clergy, religious, and seminarians in Montevideo’s cathedral, Pope Leo invited bishops worldwide to promote days of prayer and fasting for vocations to the priesthood and consecrated life. He pointed to Uruguay’s example after the interdiocesan seminary received no new candidates in 2024 and thanked those who have since begun formation. He praised long service with the line that hands grown old doing good are beautiful, and recalled Blessed Jacinto Vera, Uruguay’s first bishop, whose body rests in the cathedral.

In the same Plaza Independencia address, Pope Leo briefly addressed technology and artificial intelligence in light of work and human dignity. Citing Saint John Paul II’s Laborem Exercens, he said work is for man and not man for work, and that the development of these technologies ought to expand human capabilities, facilitate tasks, and create new possibilities while ensuring the laborer is not reduced to a mere expendable cog in the production process.

Pope Leo XIV landed in Montevideo, Uruguay, at about 4:19 p.m. local time on November 6, beginning his 12-day apostolic journey to Uruguay, Argentina, and Peru about three weeks after lung-cancer surgery. President Yamandú Orsi greeted him at Carrasco International Airport; the day’s program continues with a Plaza Independencia welcome, a meeting with the president, and Vespers at the Metropolitan Cathedral.

Aboard the flight from Rome, Pope Leo told journalists he “had no doubt” the South America trip should go ahead and said he was in “fairly good shape,” advising people facing cancer not to be afraid and to seek early detection. He formally introduced Maria Montserrat Alvarado as the new prefect of the Dicastery for Communication and said he is “proud to be American and to exercise the right to vote.”

Pope Leo XIV chose the theme for the 35th World Day of the Sick on Feb. 11, 2027: "They lowered him on the stretcher in front of Jesus: The role of the community in caring for every person," drawn from Luke 5:19. The Dicastery for Promoting Integral Human Development said Christian communities and civil society are called to care for the sick, the elderly, and those who suffer, creating spaces of closeness and hope.

As Pope Leo XIV flew toward Uruguay to open his 12-day Latin America journey, Montevideo prepared a full day-one welcome: arrival at Carrasco Airport about 4:30 p.m. local time, a ceremony in Plaza Independencia, a meeting with President Yamandú Orsi, and Vespers at the Metropolitan Cathedral. Organizers expect about 60,000 people at Saturday's youth prayer vigil in Centenario Stadium, with an outside screen for overflow; Uruguay's visit motto is "I bring you good news of great joy."

In New Orleans, the Archdiocese's Black Saints Celebration is set for Saturday, Nov. 7, with a 10 a.m. parade from Brother Martin High School to St. Martin de Porres Church for an 11:30 a.m. prayer service. Archbishop James Checchio will preside under the theme "Honoring Our Roots, Celebrating Our Faith: Many Tribes, One Spirit."

Pope Leo XIV departed Rome on Friday morning for a 12-day apostolic journey to Uruguay, Argentina, and Peru, his first return to Latin America as pope and about three weeks after lung-cancer surgery. The ITA Airways flight left Fiumicino at 7:05 a.m. Rome time; Uruguay is the first stop, with Peru the longest homecoming leg, including Chiclayo where he once served as bishop.

California Gov. Gavin Newsom, who identifies as Catholic, commuted all 548 death sentences in the state to life without parole. Catholic Mobilizing Network called the move a historic witness for life and human dignity, citing the Catechism's teaching that the death penalty is inadmissible.

After the Nov. 5 execution of Jeffrey Weisheit in his diocese, Bishop Robert McClory of Gary said Church teaching upholds the dignity of every human life, including those who commit grave crimes. He had prayed outside Indiana State Prison and pointed to the Catechism and recent papal teaching.

OSV News reports growing parish use of AI for flyers and promotions. Catholic technologists and the Diocese of Little Rock see real promise when tools are used carefully with disclosure, while others warn against generic or misleading images and urge human care in parish outreach.

The Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith upheld Bishop Douglas Deshotel's 2024 excommunication of former permanent deacon Scott Peyton of Lafayette, Louisiana, after he left for an Anglican congregation following his son's abuse by a priest. Peyton plans to appeal further; the priest's prison release is set for Nov. 14.

Pope Leo XIV sent a video message to a Rome conference marking 100 years since the consecration of the first Chinese bishops, urging Catholics to preserve unity in diversity rather than uniformity and recalling that the Church’s mission is not colonialism. On the sidelines, Cardinal Pietro Parolin said the 2018 Vatican-China agreement is imperfect but that the Holy See is “moving forward, seeking to perfect what is imperfect.”
Pope Leo XIV appointed Jesuit Fr. Avelino Chicoma Bundo Chico and Professor Claudia Leal Luna as undersecretaries of the Dicastery for Promoting Integral Human Development.

Ahead of the Nov. 6–17 Apostolic Journey to Uruguay, Argentina, and Peru, Vatican News editorial director Andrea Tornielli framed the trip as a homecoming to the continent where Leo served as a missionary and bishop, with a call to unity, evangelization, and care for the poor and vulnerable.

In a Clarion Herald column for Vocations Awareness Week, Archbishop James Checchio of New Orleans thanked the archdiocese’s priests, noted the Catholic Community Foundation’s Saint John Paul II Award to all priests of the archdiocese at its 50th-anniversary dinner, and asked the faithful to pray for priestly vocations.

The Clarion Herald profiled Archdiocese of New Orleans priests serving as military chaplains, including Fr. Kurt Young (Navy/Marine Forces Reserve), Fr. Matthew Johnston (Louisiana Army National Guard), and Fr. Andrew Sanchez (Navy, Camp Pendleton), marking more than 250 years of U.S. military chaplaincy.

Pope Leo XIV celebrated Mass in St. Peter's Basilica for the seven cardinals and 136 bishops who died over the past year, saying that praying for the dead is to celebrate life and that in Christ death does not dissolve our bonds. Afterward he prayed at the tombs of his predecessors in the Vatican Grottoes, including Pius XII, St. Paul VI and Benedict XVI.

The theme for the 2027 World Day of the Sick, to be marked on February 11, is "They lowered him on the stretcher in front of Jesus: The role of the community in caring for every person," calling parishes and civil society to care for the lonely, the elderly and the suffering.

Ahead of the Pope's November 6-17 journey to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, Cardinal Secretary of State Pietro Parolin described the visit as a witness to unity and reconciliation that will be filled with memories, affection and gratitude.

The Priestly Fraternity of Saint Peter, dedicated to the traditional Latin Mass, reported a record 25 ordinations in 2026 and now counts more than 600 members, according to its annual All Saints' Day statistics.

A 2.3 million pound restoration of Nottingham Cathedral's Pugin decorations is nearing completion, with three chapels and three ambulatories restored and Gothic decoration uncovered beneath layers of grey paint.

Fr Bashar Fawadleh, parish priest of Taybeh, the last Christian village in the West Bank, told UK parliamentarians and journalists about settler attacks on homes, cars and olive groves, and said 16 families have left the village in the past three years. His visit was hosted by the Equestrian Order of the Holy Sepulchre.

Cardinal Oswald Gracias, archbishop emeritus of Bombay, said in an interview published November 2 that he would not favor prohibiting the Traditional Latin Mass as long as it does not signal a rejection of the Second Vatican Council. He noted he had allowed it in three Bombay parishes and said there is value in the present approach of greater openness.

The Catholic University of Uruguay will host Pope Leo XIV's meeting with the world of education on Saturday, November 7. Its Jesuit rector, Fr Julio Fernández Techera, said the university has spent three years studying artificial intelligence in education, drawing on the encyclical Magnifica humanitas, and that the key message is the centrality of the human person and using the technology ethically.

Virginia's bishops responded on Nov. 4 after voters approved state constitutional amendments on abortion and same-sex marriage. Bishop Michael Burbidge of Arlington and Bishop Barry Knestout of Richmond urged Catholics to keep defending human life and marriage, and Burbidge thanked those who worked in the Catholics Vote No campaign.

The popemobile for Pope Leo XIV's visit to Peru was presented and blessed by Cardinal Pedro Barreto at the apostolic nunciature in Lima on Nov. 4. General Motors adapted two Chevrolet Colorado trucks in 24 days, adding a retractable stairway and a removable cabin.

The Diocese of Rome opens the diocesan inquiry for the beatification cause of Servant of God Lorenzo Cuneo on Friday, Nov. 6, with Cardinal Vicar Baldo Reina presiding. Cuneo, a scout leader and Caritas volunteer, was killed at 28 in 1998 when a truck struck him as he stopped to help a stranded driver on the A1 motorway.

The Museum of the Bible in Washington has opened an exhibit on Blessed Stanley Rother, the Oklahoma missionary priest martyred in Guatemala in 1981, including belongings he had the night he was killed. It runs through Oct. 1, 2027, and an EWTN Studios film on his life is due next summer.

Pope Leo XIV received Bob Dylan in a brief private audience at the Apostolic Palace on November 4. The Pope gave the singer a rosary and Dylan gave him his memoir, Chronicles: Volume One. Leo had quoted Dylan's 1963 song Go Away You Bomb in a preface on disarmament earlier this year.

Ahead of the November 6-17 trip to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, the Holy See Press Office said Pope Leo is clinically fit to travel about three weeks after his lung surgery, with no schedule changes. The trip includes nine public Masses, two stadium vigils and about 36 speeches.

Pope Leo named two new auxiliary bishops for the Archdiocese of Guadalajara, Mexico: Ramón Duarte Miranda and Héctor Michel Figeroa. The archdiocese will now have four auxiliaries while Cardinal José Francisco Robles Ortega, 77, remains archbishop.

Syro-Malabar Major Archbishop Raphael Thattil has dissolved the special tribunal created in 2024 to discipline Ernakulam-Angamaly priests who resisted the uniform liturgy, after the Apostolic Signatura suspended its cases. Suspensions on two priests were also revoked earlier this year.
A Spanish priest, Fr. Fernando Fernández de Bobadilla, described giving general absolution and helping medics at the October 28 high-speed train crash near Urda, Toledo, which killed 69 people.

Chile's foreign ministry said President José Antonio Kast and Pope Leo XIV discussed the opportunities of artificial intelligence at the service of people and the common good during their Vatican meeting on November 4.

At his last general audience before the Nov. 6-17 trip to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, Pope Leo XIV reflected on Gaudium et Spes and economic and political life. He said politics that tends the wounds of peoples and of those who suffer injustice gives hope, called unemployment, exploitation and unsafe working conditions unacceptable, and urged Christian communities to revive formation in the Church's social doctrine.

Before the audience, Pope Leo received Chilean President José Antonio Kast, who then met Archbishop Paul Richard Gallagher. The Holy See said talks touched on the Church's contribution to Chilean life, migration and demographic decline.

Meeting L'Œuvre d'Orient and the Institut Chrétiens d'Orient, which support Eastern Christians, the Pope asked them to serve a peace that is "unarmed and disarming, humble and persevering," especially in the Middle East and Eastern Europe.

The German-speaking bishops have opened public consultation on revising the 1975 German missal, with trial texts in selected parishes from Ash Wednesday to June 2027 and a target date of 2033. Liturgical Institute director Marius Linnenborn said the language should be as inclusive as possible; the text still needs the bishops' approval and the Vatican's recognitio.

Cardinal Luis Antonio Tagle told Asian Church communicators in Macau that the Church supports media technology but digital evangelization must rest on real relationships and human dignity, not manipulation. Speakers also urged using AI to serve human dignity and more support for young digital evangelizers.
The Laudato Si' Action Platform launched a Digital Atlas that maps Catholic institutions' ecological plans alongside climate and environmental data, searchable by country or diocese.

Archbishop Eamon Martin of Armagh has been elected a vice president of the Council of European Bishops' Conferences (CCEE) for 2026 to 2031, alongside Archbishop Dražen Kutleša of Zagreb, at the plenary assembly in Salzburg on October 27 to 30. Archbishop Gintaras Grušas of Vilnius was re-elected president.

The Vietnamese bishops' youth committee gathered 120 youth directors, bishops, religious, and lay leaders from 23 dioceses in Nha Trang on October 28 to 29 to plan youth ministry for the AI era. Bishop Peter Nguyen Van Vien urged leaders to listen and accompany young people, and the assembly committed to building AI ethics, media literacy, and Scripture-centered mentorship into diocesan youth ministry ahead of World Youth Day Seoul 2027.

Pope Leo XIV released his November prayer video, asking Catholics to pray for the proper use of wealth, so that money, time and talents become instruments of fraternity and service to the poor rather than selfish accumulation.

The Diocese of Knoxville issued an instruction on the SSPX after an unauthorized Latin Mass mission opened there. It says attachment to the Traditional Latin Mass is not itself schism, but liturgical preference cannot override communion with the Pope and bishops, invites those involved to reconcile, and notes an authorized monthly 1962 Missal Mass continues at a retreat center in Benton.

In Culiacan, Mexico, Father Clemente Morales Topete is recovering after being abducted on Oct. 24 and held three days, beaten, burned and threatened for information he did not have. Bishop Jesus Jose Herrera Quinonez is pressing authorities for results amid ongoing Sinaloa violence.

Church and AI: the Builders AI Forum meets Nov. 5-6 at the Pontifical Gregorian University in Rome, gathering technologists, investors and Church leaders to build AI tools for evangelization, Catholic education and healthcare grounded in human dignity. Last year's edition drew a message from Pope Leo.

The U.S. Supreme Court heard arguments on Nov. 3 in St. Mary Catholic Parish v. Roy, in which the Archdiocese of Denver and two parishes challenge their exclusion from Colorado's universal preschool program over its nondiscrimination rule. Several justices appeared sympathetic to the Catholic preschools.

Ahead of Pope Leo XIV's Nov. 6-17 journey to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, the Holy See Press Office briefed journalists and the Vatican released Church statistics for the three countries, which together count nearly 77 million baptized Catholics. The trip includes a return to Chiclayo, where he was bishop from 2015 to 2023.

Papal almoner Archbishop Luis Marin de San Martin visited Ukraine Oct. 27-30, delivering aid to 12 Catholic charitable institutions and helping distribute bread to about 2,000 people outside the cathedral in Zaporizhzhia, roughly 12 miles from the front line.

Bishop Georg Batzing of Limburg, former chair of the German bishops' conference, publicly criticized Pope Leo XIV's September remarks on abuse, asking the Pope to acknowledge that Church structures facilitated abuse and its cover-up.

Magisterium AI launched Catholic Intelligence, a platform for dioceses and parishes that keeps Mass times, ministries and pastoral letters current so the AI can steer people asking about returning to the Church, becoming Catholic or baptism toward a real parish nearby.

Pope Leo XIV released his message for the 2026 World Youth Day, celebrated in dioceses on Nov. 22, the Solemnity of Christ the King. He urges young people not to wait until they are perfect to open their lives to Christ, to bring Him their own wounds and those dividing their societies, and to prepare their hearts for the international gathering in Seoul, Aug. 3-8, 2027.

Bishop Heiner Wilmer of Münster, chairman of the German Bishops' Conference, told Europe's bishops that the German Church wants full communion with the Pope, another sign that Germany's synodal path is adjusting under Leo XIV as the Vatican pushes back on plans for a permanent Synodal Conference.

A crucifix war memorial outside St Alban's Church in Warrington, England, was vandalised on the evening of Oct. 30, with the head knocked from the figure of Christ and an anti-Catholic message written on its plaque. Cheshire Police have released a CCTV image of a man they want to question.

Cardinal Oswald Gracias, Archbishop Emeritus of Bombay and a former member of Pope Francis's Council of Cardinals, said in an interview that he would not favor prohibiting the spread of the Traditional Latin Mass, provided it does not signal a rejection of the Second Vatican Council, and that there is value in the present approach of greater openness. He said he had permitted the older rite in three Bombay churches but found it hard to find priests well versed in Latin.

The Bishops' Conference of England and Wales said war and conflict "are not inevitabilities." In a joint statement for UN Disarmament Week, Bishop Nicholas Hudson and Bishop William Kenney urged political leaders to pursue dialogue and meaningful disarmament and asked Catholics to stand together for peace.

On the eve of the US midterm elections, Catholics are working for peace at the polls. The Franciscan Action Network is sending about 375 trained poll chaplains in several dozen states to offer a calm, de-escalating presence outside polling places, and a San Diego parish held a Eucharistic procession to a ballot box. The US bishops are urging Catholics to prayerfully discern their choices and vote.

Archbishop Timothy Broglio of the Archdiocese for the Military Services told America that moral injury is a growing pastoral concern for service members, including drone operators who fight from a distance. His archdiocese is preparing presentations to help military chaplains recognize and respond to it. On AI-driven warfare, he said the Church is applying the moral principles that have always guided it, starting, as Pope Leo's Magnifica Humanitas does, with the dignity of the human person.

More than 300 young Hebrew- and Arabic-speaking Catholics gathered in the Holy Land over the weekend for a youth festival organized by the St James Vicariate of the Latin Patriarchate of Jerusalem, praying together in both languages as a sign of unity amid conflict.

Pope Leo XIV celebrated the All Souls' Day Mass at Rome's Campo Verano Cemetery, saying that faith in Christ means our bond with the dead is not broken but transformed. Calling the Beatitudes the path to a full life now and in eternity, he prayed especially for those whose loved ones were torn away by the senseless violence of war, asking that their tears touch the consciences of those with the power to silence the weapons.

Four priests were ordained Oct. 31 for the Society of the Missionaries of Divine Mercy, a traditional French community, by Bishop François Touvet at the Benedictine Abbey of Notre-Dame de Triors. The society had waited since 2022, when the Vatican halted diocesan ordinations, for confirmation that its new priests could offer the traditional Mass under Traditionis Custodes.

Poland's bishops have appealed for dialogue and prayer as a standoff over the country's Constitutional Tribunal deepens. The bishops' conference presidium said it is not the Church's role to judge the dispute, but asked politicians to calm the conflict and seek a peaceful resolution, warning of a deep crisis of the state.

The Maronite Archeparchy of Haifa condemned the vandalizing of the Saints Peter and Paul prayer hall in Nahariya, northern Israel, on All Saints' Day, where statues were broken and religious images defaced. Archbishop Moussa El-Hage called it a grave attack on freedom of worship and asked police to find those responsible, adding that the community will keep praying there and will not answer evil with hatred.

New York Archbishop Ronald Hicks has joined the lawsuit by the Little Sisters of the Poor, other religious orders, Bishop John Barres of Rockville Centre and ArchCare challenging New York's new assisted suicide law, which a federal court has already barred the state from enforcing against the Catholic plaintiffs while the case proceeds. "We refuse to allow New York to force us to harm the very ones we've been called to care for," he said.

The Diocese of Rome will open the sainthood cause of Lorenzo Cuneo on Nov. 6 at the Lateran Palace. A scout and Caritas volunteer who served the homeless of Rome and war-torn families in the Balkans, he was killed at 28 by a truck after stopping to help a driver in trouble on the A1 motorway.

The Diocese of Macau, the first modern diocese created in Asia, closed its 450th-anniversary celebrations on October 31 with a pontifical Mass at the Forum de Macau presided over by Cardinal Luis Antonio Tagle. Thousands of faithful attended, and Cardinal Tagle called the jubilee an act of thanksgiving for a living faith that must keep moving forward. The jubilee year continues through January 2027.

Pope Leo XIV celebrates Mass for All Souls' Day this afternoon at 4 p.m. Rome time at the city's Verano Cemetery, as he did in 2025. On Thursday, November 5, he will offer Mass in St. Peter's Basilica for the cardinals and bishops who died this past year, before leaving on November 6 for his South America trip to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru.

Oleshky evacuees reached Ukraine and reunited with family under a six-day local ceasefire brokered with help from U.S. First Lady Melania Trump and Pope Leo XIV's appeals. The Pope welcomed the operation at Sunday's Angelus and hoped it would lead to new peace initiatives; the truce was due to expire by Monday, and some residents chose to stay.

In Savannah, Archbishop Gregory Hartmayer of Atlanta presided at an All Saints' Day Mass of thanksgiving for the five newly beatified Georgia Martyrs, Franciscan friars killed in 1597, saying they are on their way to being saints. Bishop Stephen Parkes said the diocese will keep their memorial on Sept. 22.

The Asian bishops' communications office (FABC-OSC) closed its Macau meeting with a statement calling AI a gift and an opportunity that must serve communion. It commits to AI literacy, pastoral AI policies in each bishops' conference, putting papal and Church documents online in local languages so AI tools represent the faith accurately, and a regional committee to train digital missionaries, while warning about deepfakes, cyber-scam trafficking and AI replacing human presence and prayer.

Peru's Church is mourning a second bishop in under 48 hours. Bishop Jorge Pedro Carrión Pavlich of Puno, 76, died in Lima, two days after Cusco's Archbishop Richard Alarcón. He led Puno for more than 24 years. The funeral Mass is Tuesday, Nov. 3, in Puno, with burial in his hometown of Tarma on Nov. 4. Pope Leo XIV is due in Peru Nov. 11-16.

New Orleans marked All Saints' Day with its traditional cemetery blessings, a French Catholic custom of blessing graves on Nov. 1. Archbishop James Checchio, celebrating his first All Saints' Day as archbishop, offered an 11 a.m. Mass at Our Lady of the Rosary and blessed the graves at St. Louis Cemetery No. 3, with evening Masses at Loyola and the Tulane Catholic Center.

France ordered stepped-up protection of churches and Christian cemeteries for All Saints' and All Souls'. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez cited a very high terror threat level and 843 anti-Christian acts recorded in 2025, up 9 percent, mostly property damage and largely affecting Catholic sites.

At the All Saints Angelus, Pope Leo XIV said holiness is not a privilege for a few but a universal vocation, made of choices of love that rise above greed and evil, and urged the faithful never to grow weary of fostering peace in great and ordinary situations alike.

After the Angelus, the Pope welcomed this week's evacuation of hundreds of civilians from the Russian-occupied Ukrainian town of Oleshky under a rare humanitarian ceasefire and hoped the cooperation behind it would lead to dialogue. He also recalled the newly beatified Georgia Martyrs, greeted athletes at the Youth Olympic Games in Senegal, pointed to the coming World Day of the Poor, and asked for prayers for the dead.

In New Orleans, St. Augustine High School, the Josephite-run Catholic school, beat Edna Karr 52-14 before more than 18,000 fans, ending Karr's 35-game winning streak and clinching a share of the Catholic League title, with Archbishop Rummel next on Friday.

Pope Leo XIV sent condolences on the death of Archbishop Richard Alarcón Urrutia of Cusco, calling him a selfless pastor and entrusting him to Our Lady of Bethlehem. The archbishop died Oct. 30 at 74, and his funeral is set for Nov. 1 in Cusco's cathedral. The Pope said he hopes to pray with the local Church during his Nov. 15 visit, and Archbishop Lizardo Estrada Herrera now leads the archdiocese.

AI scientist Gary Marcus, who attended the Oct. 30 Vatican meeting on the future of AI, called Pope Leo XIV the clearest thinker on AI among prominent world leaders and endorsed all five points of his address, from keeping humans responsible for life-and-death decisions to building international oversight. Marcus says he is now a global ambassador for the encyclical Magnifica Humanitas through the Domus Communis Foundation.

Pope Leo XIV accepted the resignation of Archbishop Aldo Cavalli as Special Apostolic Visitator for the parish of Medjugorje and named Bishop Francesco Cavina, emeritus of Carpi, to the post for an indefinite period. The same bulletin named Fr. Martial Bernard, vicar general of Évry-Corbeil-Essonnes, as bishop of Soissons, France.

Aid to the Church in Need's new report, Persecuted and Forgotten? 2024-26, finds conditions for Christians worsened in about 55 percent of the 18 countries studied, with none improving. The pontifical charity estimates 413 million Christians live where religious freedom is seriously violated and about 220 million face direct persecution, citing displacement in Africa and Asia, authoritarian pressure in places like Nicaragua and Iran, and religious nationalism in India.

items.text: Cardinal Luis Antonio Tagle, preaching at the 75th anniversary Mass of the Diocese of Legazpi in the Philippines, said homilies must come from personal faith and an encounter with Christ rather than from AI, which he described as a reorganizing of existing data. He added that technology and social media can support evangelization but cannot replace human witnesses, echoing Pope Leo XIV's February remarks to the clergy of Rome.

Five Spanish Franciscan friars killed in 1597 while serving the Guale people on the Georgia coast, known as the Georgia Martyrs, were beatified in Savannah on Saturday, October 31. Cardinal Frank Leo of Toronto presided as papal legate and called them shining witnesses of the Gospel.

Papal Almoner Archbishop Luis Marín de San Martín closed his charity mission to Ukraine on October 30 with stops in Kyiv and Fastiv, visiting a Missionaries of Charity shelter and meeting mothers who lost children in the war, after a night of missile and drone attacks on the capital.

Louisiana's Fifth Circuit Court of Appeal dismissed a wrongful-death lawsuit against the Archdiocese of New Orleans brought by the mother of a 17-year-old Archbishop Rummel High School student who died by suicide hours after being expelled. The court found the facts did not fit any theory of liability; the mother's attorney says she will appeal.

Bishop Fintan Monahan of Killaloe, Ireland, defended his diocese's use of AI-generated images of Jesus, the four evangelists and local saints in feast-day and daily Gospel posts after some parishioners objected. He told Clare FM the tool is used under strict guidelines and is meant to complement, not replace, human pastoral contact.

Pope Leo XIV met Saturday with representatives of towns in Lazio, Marche, Umbria and Abruzzo hit by the 2016-2017 Central Italy earthquakes, which killed about 300 people. Ten years on, about 10,000 people still live in temporary housing. The Pope urged that reconstruction move as quickly, safely and transparently as possible, built on shared responsibility and a vision that starts again from God, people and the common good.

Archbishop Paul Gallagher, the Vatican foreign minister, said a papal visit to the United States is very likely in the not-too-distant future, possibly 2027 or later, with timing shaped by the U.S. election calendar. He said Pope Leo is going ahead with his Nov. 6-17 trip to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru because he wants to go, given positive reports after his lung surgery.

Pope Leo chose "The love of Christ sends us forth," from St. Paul's Second Letter to the Corinthians, as the theme for the 101st World Mission Day on Oct. 24, 2027. His message for the day will be published early next year.

Fr. Fernando Fernández de Bobadilla, pastor of Los Yébenes in Spain, described giving general absolution aloud to the dead and dying at the Oct. 28 high-speed train collision near Urda (Toledo), then staying to comfort the injured and help rescue workers. He said the experience showed him how beautiful it is to be a priest in such painful circumstances.

Paolo Ruffini, the first layperson to head a Roman Curia office, ends his eight-year term as Prefect of the Dicastery for Communication on October 31. Staff bid him farewell on October 30. Montserrat Alvarado, formerly president and chief operating officer of EWTN News, takes office on November 1 as the first laywoman to lead a Curia dicastery.

Pope Leo XIV holds a private audience on Saturday in the Paul VI Hall with the basketball teams of his alma mater Villanova and of Notre Dame, plus traveling fans, about 7,000 people in all, ahead of the two schools' season opener in Rome.

Archbishop Peter Machado of Bengaluru, joined by Muslim and civil society leaders, urged Karnataka's government on October 30 to fully repeal the state's 2022 anti-conversion law rather than amend it, and to strengthen hate-speech laws. A rally is planned for November 9 at Freedom Park.

Archbishop Richard Daniel Alarcón Urrutia of Cusco, Peru, died on October 30 at age 74 after a battle with cancer, just over two weeks before Pope Leo XIV is due in Cusco on November 15. Coadjutor Archbishop Lizardo Estrada Herrera now takes full leadership of the archdiocese.

EWTN is shutting down its WEWN shortwave radio service on October 31 after 34 years, citing high costs, aging transmitters and a shrinking shortwave audience. Its programming will keep reaching Africa, the Middle East and Latin America through more than 600 AM/FM affiliates, satellite, streaming and apps.

The Diocese of Savannah expects about 10,000 people on Saturday, October 31, for the beatification of the five Franciscan Georgia martyrs killed in 1597, only the sixth beatification held in the United States. The Mass will be celebrated at the Savannah convention center.

Pope Leo XIV has approved amendments to the personnel regulations of the Roman Curia in a rescript dated October 19. The changes clarify who may suspend an employee (office heads up to 30 days, the Curia's Disciplinary Commission for longer), fix a mismatch in the deadlines for presenting a defense that had led to some proceedings being voided, and address access to legal assistance.

Closing their plenary assembly in Salzburg, the Council of European Bishops' Conferences appealed for a just and lasting peace in Ukraine and other war zones, saying true peace cannot be imposed and begins in the human heart. The assembly confirmed Archbishop Gintaras Grušas of Vilnius as president for 2026-2031 and elected Archbishop Eamon Martin of Armagh and Archbishop Dražen Kutleša of Zagreb as vice-presidents.

At the Asian bishops' social communication assembly in Macau, Radio Veritas Asia's Gethsemani Cindy Gorospe asked bishops' conferences to bring young Catholic digital missionaries into pastoral life, proposing a dedicated FABC committee and formation in theology, spiritual resilience and communication ahead of World Youth Day 2027 in Seoul. Speakers also urged that AI be directed toward human dignity and lasting relationships.

Valerie Pisano, president and CEO of Mila, the Quebec Artificial Intelligence Institute, told Vatican News that more people need to get involved in shaping AI so its development is directed toward the good of humanity.

Pope Leo XIV addressed a Vatican meeting on the future of AI, organized by the Pontifical Academy for Life and the Future of Life Institute. He said AI's future is not pre-determined and depends on human choices, that machines are tools and not persons and should not be given legal personhood, that decisions over life and the use of force must stay under human oversight, and that AI's benefits should be shared with those most in need. He urged states meeting in Geneva in November to move toward banning lethal autonomous weapons and called for international institutions with shared standards and independent oversight.

The Holy See confirmed that Pope Leo XIV has submitted his mail-in ballot in Chicago for the U.S. midterm elections, making him the first pope to vote in an American election. The statement said he has voted whenever eligible, including during his years in Peru, and believes in the right and duty of citizens to take part in democratic processes.

Pope Leo XIV named two new undersecretaries of the General Secretariat of the Synod: Fr. Giacomo Costa, SJ, who served as special secretary of recent synod assemblies, and Salesian Sr. Elena Massimi, FMA, a professor of liturgy and sacramental theology at the Pontifical Salesian University.

Pope Leo XIV has requested a mail-in ballot for the November 3 U.S. midterm elections in Illinois, the Chicago Sun-Times reported. He is registered under his baptismal name, Robert Francis Prevost, at an address in New Lenox, home to an Augustinian parish and high school. The ballot was requested on October 3.

Church and AI: At the Asian bishops' communications assembly in Macau on October 29, Bishop Marcelino Antonio Maralit Jr. of San Pablo, Philippines, called the digital world "the main square, the Areopagus of our time" for the Church in Asia and urged an ethical, person-centered use of AI. He proposed pastoral guidelines on transparency, data privacy and seminary formation, cautioned priests not to pass off AI-written homilies as their own, and concluded that "behind every screen in Asia, there is a face."

The Vatican Museums opened "A Century of the Popemobile," showing eight historic Mercedes-Benz papal cars, from the 1930 Nürburg 460 given to Pius XI to the modern Popemobiles. It runs in the Square Garden through January 31, 2027, included with museum admission.

Pope Leo XIV visits Uruguay November 6 to 8, the first papal visit there in nearly 38 years. Bishop Arturo Fajardo of Salto, ordained a priest by St. John Paul II in 1988, said he hopes the visit will help baptized Catholics who have drifted rediscover the joy of the faith.

Cardinal Luis Cabrera of Guayaquil, Ecuador, announced a technical safety review of church buildings and parish houses across the archdiocese's 161 parishes, with the fire department, after Redemptorist Father Patricio Sánchez Molinari was killed on October 17 when a cross fell on him during Mass. The collection at Saturday's Mass marking 100 years of the city's Christ the King feast will go to victims of El Niño flooding.

The International Catholic Migration Commission, founded in 1951 under Pius XII, marks its 75th anniversary with a Council meeting in Rome on November 10 to 12 to elect a new president and adopt a four-year strategy. Cardinal Fabio Baggio and former UN refugee chief Filippo Grandi are among the speakers.

A report that the Summorum Pontificum pilgrimage will be barred from using Rome's Augustinianum for future gatherings has been denied by Christian Marquant, president of the coalition that organizes it, who said the group never asked for the venue for 2027 and nothing was refused. The report came from a Messainlatino editor recounting a conversation; the separate refusal of a Pontifical Mass in St. Peter's this year still stands.

Speaking at the Vatican's International Congress for Pastoral Care in Schools and Universities on October 23, Cardinal Timothy Radcliffe urged educators to meet young people in the age of AI by inviting questions, wonder and adventure. He called for a new vision of work that is about being human, rooted in the kind of loving attention to others that no AI can give.

Archbishop Luis Marín de San Martín, prefect of the Dicastery for the Service of Charity, is visiting Ukraine on Pope Leo XIV's behalf. In Kyiv he met volunteers and Church communities providing hot meals and shelter to people affected by the war.

At the UN General Assembly on Oct. 28, the Holy See's Permanent Observer, Archbishop Christophe El Kassis, called outer space a common good that must stay a realm of peace and cooperation, and urged that its exploration benefit all peoples, including developing countries, without creating new inequalities.

Ahead of the U.S. midterm elections, the USCCB released videos in which Archbishops Alexander Sample, William Lori and Shelton Fabre urge Catholics to form their consciences in faith first. Sample said Catholics are disciples of Jesus first, Americans second, and party members third, and Lori stressed that faithful citizenship is not a voter guide.
In Urda, Spain, parish priest Fr. José Miguel Fernández, who spent hours with victims of Wednesday's high-speed train collision, celebrated a Mass for the dead and their families.

Church and AI: Bishop Watterson High School in Columbus, Ohio, held a full day of faculty formation titled Faithfully Forward: Navigating AI in Catholic Education, joined by teachers from its Catholic feeder schools.

Pope Leo XIV sent a telegram, signed by Cardinal Parolin and addressed to Archbishop Francisco Cerro Chaves of Toledo, expressing deep sorrow after two high-speed trains collided in Urda, central Spain, on Wednesday. The provisional death toll stands at 68, with 53 still hospitalized; the Pope prayed for the dead, comforted families, and encouraged rescue teams.

Costa Rican President Laura Fernández Delgado met Pope Leo XIV at the Vatican on Oct. 29 and invited him to visit Costa Rica, which has not hosted a pope since St. John Paul II in 1983. Talks with Cardinal Parolin and Archbishop Gallagher covered security and migration, especially Nicaraguan migrants.

Organisers of the Ad Petri Sedem Latin Mass pilgrimage moved to settle confusion over last weekend in Rome. They say the one-hour Mass at St. Mary Major and its no-photography rule were agreed in advance and were not last-minute restrictions, while the Secretariat of State's refusal of a Mass and a group procession in St. Peter's still stands.

In National Catholic Reporter, Chicago high school senior Leo Fiascone describes building a bilingual citizenship-test study platform for Erie Neighborhood House, including a 24/7 AI tutor called Benji. He says he took Magnifica Humanitas as a call to aim AI at people often left behind; the tool supports human tutors rather than replacing them and is being shared with other Chicago groups.

At the FABC Office of Social Communication assembly in Macau (Oct. 27-31), themed on Magnifica Humanitas and communicating Christ in the age of AI, Bishop Malcolm Sequeira of Amravati, India, told Asian Catholic communicators that AI should be a tool, not their armor. "Be assured. Be fearless. Do not panic," he said, noting the Church has always put the tools of each era at the service of the Gospel.

In Rome, the Ad Bonum Facere Foundation, formed by Poor Clare, Capuchin Poor Clare, Benedictine and Discalced Carmelite monasteries, held its first course on women's monasteries in the age of AI. Fr. Philip Larrey told Vatican News that AI has little place in contemplative prayer but can help cloistered communities with practical work such as legal, administrative and supply tasks, provided sources are checked; he pointed to Magisterium AI's citations as a good example.

Six young Christian men in Egypt, aged 17 to 23, were released after more than two weeks in prison over a TikTok video authorities called offensive to Islam, but they still face charges of exploiting and insulting religion.

Bishop Carlos Herrera, president of Nicaragua's bishops' conference, confirmed the Holy See has postponed their ad limina visit to next year, citing a lack of “appropriate conditions.” Four of the ten bishops are already in exile, and priests say the others fear they wouldn't be allowed back in.
Cardinal Parolin opened the Gregorian University's conference on the Holy See and 20th-century totalitarian regimes, warning that some still want to “control how humanity lives and thinks.”

In New Orleans, Archbishop Checchio's November Clarion Herald column turns to All Saints and All Souls, Blessed Francis Xavier Seelos, and Servant of God Henriette Delille, and asks the faithful to pray for their own dead this month.
